subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Tesla Roadster
description: Learn The Tesla Roadster in one minute.

hook.text: Tesla's first car was based on a Lotus Elise body—light, nimble, and stripped to the essentials.

buildup.text: It packed 6,831 lithium-ion laptop cells into the floor. Nobody had tried that approach at scale.

discovery.text: The Roadster hit 60 mph in under 4 seconds and had a 245-mile range—unheard of for an EV.

twist.text: Production was a nightmare. Costs overran massively and Tesla nearly went bankrupt multiple times.

climax.text: Only 2,450 were built, but they proved one thing: electric cars could be genuinely desirable.

punchline.text: The Roadster sold a feeling, not just a technology.

quiz.question: How many original Tesla Roadsters were built?

details.summary: The original Tesla Roadster, launched in 2008, was the first highway-legal production electric car using lithium-ion batteries, proving that EVs could deliver sports car performance with over 200 miles of range.
details.whyItMatters: The Roadster shattered the golf-cart image of electric vehicles. By building a fast, desirable sports car first, Tesla established credibility and attracted the investment needed to build mass-market EVs.
takeaways: It was based on a modified Lotus Elise chassis
Range of 244 miles per charge was revolutionary for 2008
About 2,450 Roadsters were sold before production ended in 2012

faq.question: How did the Roadster prove EVs could be desirable?
faq.answer: It accelerated from zero to sixty in 3.7 seconds with a 244-mile range, matching or beating gasoline sports cars. Celebrity buyers and positive reviews made it aspirational, destroying the perception that EVs were slow and boring.

faq.question: Was the first Tesla Roadster profitable?
faq.answer: Barely. Tesla nearly went bankrupt multiple times during Roadster production. The car was more a proof of concept than a profitable product, but it attracted the attention and investment needed to fund the Model S and beyond.
